canonicalExplanation.summary: A React project is reproducible when anyone can clone it, run `npm ci`, and get **the same dependency versions** from the **lockfile** (`package-lock.json`). `package.json` lists what you depend on; the lockfile pins exactly which versions were installed, so commit both. With Vite, `index.html` loads `src/main.jsx`, the **one entry path** that creates the root. `npm run dev` is a fast development server, but **`npm run build` is what users get**: an optimised production bundle. Only variables prefixed `VITE_` reach browser code, and they are public. Check the production build with `npm run preview` before shipping.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A teammate clones your React project and gets a blank page. You had upgraded a library locally without committing the lockfile, and the production build also fails on a code path the dev server never touched. A Vite project renders under StrictMode, keeps browser-safe config explicit, and verifies a production build. In this lesson you'll create and reproduce a React project from its manifest and lockfile.

```predict
{"question": "`npm run dev` works perfectly. Is the production build guaranteed to work?", "options": ["Yes", "No: the build bundles, optimises and checks differently, so run it too"], "answer": 1, "why": "Dev and build are different pipelines. Always run `npm run build` and `npm run preview`."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know the **Modular browser application**, **Application root and rendering**, and **Dependency manifests and lockfiles** (package.json and lockfiles in version control).

sections.heading: The model: manifest, lockfile, entry, build
sections.body:
```text
my-app/
  package.json        # what we depend on + scripts.
  package-lock.json   # exact versions installed. Commit it.
  index.html          # loads /src/main.jsx.
  vite.config.js
  .env.example        # documents VITE_ variables; no secrets.
  src/
    main.jsx          # the one entry: createRoot + StrictMode.
    App.jsx
```

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "vite",
    "build": "vite build",
    "preview": "vite preview",
    "test": "vitest"
  },
  "dependencies": { "react": "19.1.0", "react-dom": "19.1.0" },
  "devDependencies": { "vite": "7.1.3", "@vitejs/plugin-react": "5.0.2", "vitest": "3.2.4" }
}
```

| Command | Use |
|---|---|
| `npm ci`. | clean install exactly from the lockfile. |
| `npm run dev`. | local development with fast refresh. |
| `npm run build`. | production bundle in dist/. |
| `npm run preview`. | serve dist/ locally to check it. |

```reveal
{"prompt": "Why `npm ci` instead of `npm install` on a fresh clone or in CI?", "answer": "npm ci installs exactly what the lockfile says and fails if package.json and the lockfile disagree, so everyone gets the same versions."}
```

examples.title: Works on my machine, and in the build
examples.situation: A Vite project renders under StrictMode, keeps browser-safe config explicit, and verifies a production build on a teammate's clone.
walkthrough: **Pin and commit:** package.json uses exact versions and package-lock.json is committed.
**One entry:** index.html loads src/main.jsx, which renders App under StrictMode; .env.example lists only VITE_API_URL.
**Verify:** on a fresh clone, `npm ci`, `npm test` and `npm run build` will all pass before anyone pushes.
examples.result: Any teammate can reproduce the same working app, and the production build is checked, not assumed.

examples.title: The secret in the bundle
examples.situation: A developer renames `API_SECRET` to `VITE_API_SECRET` because the app "couldn't read it". The secret now appears in dist/assets/index-*.js.
walkthrough: Only VITE_ variables are exposed to browser code.
Exposing means copying the value into the public bundle.
Fix: keep the secret on a server endpoint, revoke the leaked one, and search dist/ for it in CI.
examples.result: The bundle contains no secrets, and the app calls a server that holds the key.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: If the development server works, dependency and production configuration are necessarily correct.
misconceptions.correction: The dev server doesn't bundle or optimise the same way, and your machine may have different dependency versions. Reproduce with npm ci from the lockfile and run the production build to be sure.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "Works on my machine, and in the build", what two things were missing?

analogy.example: package.json is a **shopping list** ("flour, eggs"); the lockfile is the **receipt** with exact brands and sizes. To bake the same cake elsewhere you need the receipt. The dev server is **tasting while cooking**; the production build is **the cake you serve**, so taste that too.
limitations: Receipts don't update themselves; you commit the lockfile after installs.
Anything in the cake (bundle) can be seen by guests.

remediation.explanation: Before sharing a project ask: **Is the lockfile committed? Does a fresh clone with npm ci pass tests and build? Is anything secret prefixed VITE_?**
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply this to "The secret in the bundle".

recap.summary: To create and reproduce a React project from its manifest and lockfile, commit package.json and the lockfile, install with npm ci, keep one entry in main.jsx under StrictMode, expose only public VITE_ config, and run the production build and preview instead of trusting the dev server.
